Synopsis:
 Diesel and heating oil prices have spiked sharply, driven by three concurrent pressures: renewed US-Iran military hostilities raising crude oil risk premia, Russia extending its diesel export ban (compounded by Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian refineries), and broader Brent crude rallying toward $97/bbl. UK red diesel is up ~10% in days; US diesel hit a ~4-year high at $5.78/gallon. UK farmers are the focal victims — struggling with cashflow and fuel procurement timing ahead of winter land preparation. Heating oil (paraffin) prices have also surged ~67% vs. pre-war levels, hitting rural households off the gas grid particularly hard.

Iran/Hormuz escalation risk is a direct threat to LNG flows from the Gulf region.
